page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the c4 family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. This processor features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading and a large 504 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 31.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. It also includes a bundled 137 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed storage, while containing no GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of average single-core and weaker multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is average at 2240.59, whereas the multi-core score is weak at 4549.86. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth rated as poor at 22.46 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth rated as weak at 15.13 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations show strength; gzip compression is strong at 35.55 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing is strong at 2828.0. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 7.38 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is weak at 4.72 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local NVMe SSD, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity and fast local storage without needing massive multi-core compute power. It is suitable for single-threaded tasks, text processing, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight database operations. However, it is less suited for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications, multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its poor 5.04 tokens/sec text generation speed on 7B models.
